exposure: Hypertonic sodium chloride hydroxyethyl starch 40 (HSH40) as perioperative fluid therapy
cohort: Forty preeclamptic women undergoing caesarean section.
finding: Low-dose HSH40 infusion in preeclamptic women undergoing caesarean section significantly decreased plasma levels of vasoconstrictors (ET and TXB₂) and increased levels of vasodilators (6-keto-PGF1α and ANP), thereby maintaining circulatory blood volume, improving renal function, and increasing urine output.
